candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — environmental infection-control practices
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — environmental cleaning
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize routine between-procedure environmental cleaning as a required infection-prevention practice in operating rooms.

options.A: Clean only when visible soil is present or a known infection has been identified
options.B: Skip environmental cleaning if sterile technique will be used for the next case
options.C: Clean and disinfect designated environmental surfaces and noncritical equipment according to the between-procedure protocol
options.D: Perform only terminal cleaning after the final procedure of the day

candidate.rationale: CDC environmental-cleaning guidance identifies operating rooms as areas requiring environmental cleaning at three intervals: before the first procedure, between procedures, and after the last procedure. The OR section applies to environmental surfaces and surfaces of noncritical equipment; critical and semicritical equipment require separate specialized reprocessing. C is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Operating rooms require environmental cleaning between procedures; the described process covers environmental surfaces and noncritical equipment surfaces, while critical/semicritical equipment requires specialized reprocessing.
candidate.source_locator: Section 4.6.1 Operating rooms — environmental cleaning before first procedure, between procedures, and after last procedure; environmental surfaces/noncritical equipment
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.source_version_date: Current CDC healthcare environmental-cleaning webpage accessed 2026-08-17
candidate.stem: Which environmental-cleaning practice is appropriate between procedures in an operating room?
